draft.title: Genghis Khan
card: Before 1206, the Mongols were many separate tribes who lived on the grasslands of Central Asia. The tribes often fought one another.
A leader called Temujin won over or defeated the other tribes. In 1206 the Mongol chiefs named him Genghis Khan, which means a ruler of all the Mongols.
Once the tribes were united, he led them in wars of conquest. His armies took land across much of Asia, from northern China towards Central Asia and Persia.
After his death in 1227, his sons and grandsons kept expanding. The Mongol Empire became the largest land empire the world had seen.
draft.remember: Genghis Khan first united the Mongol tribes, and then led them to conquer much of Asia.

a.q: What did Genghis Khan do in 1206 that made the later conquests possible?
opts: He united the Mongol tribes under one ruler
He conquered the city of Beijing in China
He opened the Silk Roads to travellers
He made himself ruler of all of Europe
a.why: In 1206 the Mongol chiefs named Temujin as Genghis Khan, so the tribes now fought as one. Taking cities and land came later, once the tribes were united behind him.
a.clue: Think about what had to happen to the tribes before they could act together.

b.q: Before 1206, a traveller on the grasslands of Central Asia meets Mongol groups who fight each other. Why were the Mongols then not yet a danger to far-off lands?
opts: They were divided tribes and had no single leader
They had no horses and could not travel far
They already ruled the largest empire in the world
They were ruled by the Chinese emperor
b.why: Before 1206 the Mongols were separate tribes who often fought each other, so they could not act as one army. Their power grew only after Genghis Khan united them.
b.clue: Look at what changed for the tribes in 1206.

a.best: He united the Mongol tribes under one ruler

b.best: They were divided tribes and had no single leader

problems.detail: The card says 'Genghis Khan' means 'a ruler of all the Mongols'. The meaning of the title is uncertain and debated by historians. It is usually given as 'universal ruler', and sometimes as 'fierce' or 'oceanic' ruler, not as 'ruler of all the Mongols'. Better to say the title is usually translated as 'universal ruler', or that its exact meaning is uncertain.
